תִּתְבָּרַךְ צוּרֵנוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ וְגֹאֲלֵנוּ בּוֹרֵא קְדוֹשִׁים יִשְׁתַּבַּח שִׁמְךָ
לָעַד מַלְכֵּנוּ יוֹצֵר מְשָׁרְתִים וַאֲשֶׁר מְשָׁרְתָיו כֻּלָּם עוֹמְדִים
בְּרוּם עוֹלָם וּמַשְׁמִיעִים בְּיִרְאָה יַחַד בְּקוֹל דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים
וּמֶלֶךְ עוֹלָם: כֻּלָּם אֲהוּבִים כֻּלָּם בְּרוּרִים כֻּלָּם גִּבּוֹרִים
וְכֻלָּם עֹשִׂים בְּאֵימָה וּבְיִרְאָה רְצוֹן קוֹנָם וְכֻלָּם פּוֹתְחִים
אֶת־פִּיהֶם בִּקְדֻשָּׁה וּבְטָהֳרָה בְּשִׁירָה וּבְזִמְרָה וּמְבָרְכִים
וּמְשַׁבְּחִים וּמְפָאֲרִים וּמַעֲרִיצִים וּמַקְדִּישִׁים וּמַמְלִיכִים

blocks.text:
אֶת־שֵׁם הָאֵל הַמֶּלֶךְ הַגָּדוֹל הַגִּבּוֹר וְהַנּוֹרָא קָדוֹשׁ הוּא:
וְכֻלָּם מְקַבְּלִים עֲלֵיהֶם עֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם זֶה מִזֶּה. וְנוֹתְנִים
רְשׁוּת זֶה לָזֶה. לְהַקְדִּישׁ לְיוֹצְרָם בְּנַחַת רוּחַ בְּשָׂפָה בְרוּרָה
וּבִנְעִימָה קְדֻשָּׁה כֻּלָּם כְּאֶחָד עוֹנִים וְאוֹמְרִים בְּיִרְאָה.

כָּל־עֶשְׁתּוֹנוֹת צָעִיר וָרַב, מֶלֶךְ. גֵּאוּת וָעוֹז
הִתְאַזָּר מֶלֶךְ. דּוֹק וָחֶלֶד יֶחֱרְדוּן מֵאֵימַת
מֶלֶךְ:

הַיּוֹצֵר יַחַד לִבָּם יָחוֹן מֶלֶךְ. וּמֵבִין אֶל־כָּל־מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם
יַצְדִּיק מֶלֶךְ. זִכָּרוֹן הוּא יוֹם תְּרוּעַת מֶלֶךְ. ״ חֹק לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
הוּא לְזַכּוֹתָם מֶלֶךְ. טֶרֶף נָתַן לִירֵאָיו מַמְלִיךְ כָּל־מֶלֶךְ.
יִזְכּוֹר לְעוֹלָם בְּרִיתוֹ בְּזִכְרוֹן טוֹב מֶלֶךְ:

לְךָ מַלְכֵּנוּ מֶלֶךְ. מֵאֶתְמוֹל קִדַּמְנוּךָ לְחַלּוֹתְךָ

blocks.text: 39 Morning Prayer for the New Year 39

[cue: תתברך] Blessed art Thou, our Rock, our King and our Redeemer, Creator of holy beings. May Thy Name be extolled for ever, O our King, who has formed the ministering angels; and all His ministering angels stand on the summit of the world and loudly proclaim in awe together the words of the living God and King of the world. All of them are loved, all are selected, all are mighty and all perform in reverence and fear the will of their Creator. All of them open their mouth in sanctity and purity, in song and melody, and bless and praise, glorify and revere, sanctify and crown the Name of God, the great, mighty and awe-inspiring King, holy is He. And all accept upon themselves the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven, one from the other, and grant each other permission to sanctify their Creator in tranquillity of spirit with pure speech and pleasantness, they all chime the sanctification together and say in fear:
blocks.layout: one justified paragraph that opens with a Hebrew cue word; no paragraph break at 'And all accept'

blocks.text:
Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts,
The whole earth is full of His glory.

[cue: כבודו] He extends His glory this day in mercy, the King, He who tests all thoughts of small and great, the King, in majesty and might does the King gird Himself, heaven and earth quake from fear of the King.

[cue: היוצר] He who has formed together their heart, will show grace, the King. He who knows all their deeds, will justify, the King. It is a memorial, a day of homage through the Shofar sound, a law for Israel, so that the King may acquit them. Food does He give to those who fear Him, He who appoints every king, eternally does He remember His covenant in kindly memory, the King.
blocks.layout: paragraph, first line indented; 'cove-nant' is hyphenated across a line break

blocks.text: [cue: כלה] Let not destruction overtake the remnant of the King's sons (Israel), Therefore, our King, do we come before Thee. O King, yesterday did we approach Thee already to implore

uncertainties.mark: The holam on the vav of אוֹפַן and the holam on רֹאשׁ are faint. I can't tell if they are printed.
Printed with an alef-lamed ligature (the lamed ascender sits on the alef). The lamed's holam is not separately visible.
The holam is not clearly visible. It may be printed unpointed as על.
Cantillation and meteg marks are present under the first two קדוש, צבאות, מלא and הארץ. I did not transcribe them exactly. The paseq is a small vertical mark.
A small superscript double-tick sign with a dot. Its function is unclear: it could be a reader cue or a division sign.
The hiriq under the alef is hard to see.
The vowel under the het could be segol or hataf-segol.
The holam could be on the vav (וָעוֹז) or written defectively (וָעֹז).
These words are set in slightly smaller type, and I can't confirm their points.
The shin/sin dot and the patah are hard to make out.
There is a stray acute-like mark between 'fear' and 'the', probably a printing blemish. I left it out.

observations: Hebrew s106 and English s107 both carry printed page number 39 (a facing-page pair).

The Ofan is an alphabetical acrostic. The first letters run א (אִהֵל), ב (בּוֹחֵן), ג (גֵּאוּת), ד (דּוֹק) / ה (הַיּוֹצֵר), ו (וּמֵבִין), ז (זִכָּרוֹן), ח (חֹק), ט (טֶרֶף), י (יִזְכּוֹר) / כ (כָּלָה), ל (לָכֵן), מ (מֵאֶתְמוֹל), and continue on the next page. Every line ends with the refrain מֶלֶךְ.
Stanza 1 opens with the linking word כְּבוֹדוֹ, picking up the last word of the Kadosh verse. Stanzas 1 and 3 are in large type; stanza 2 is in smaller type.
The divine Name in the Kadosh verse is printed as the abbreviation יְיָ.
The English page's Hebrew opening words (תתברך, כבודו, היוצר, כלה) are cues linking it to the Hebrew page. They are marked [cue: …] and are not part of the English prayer text.
The English translation has no counterpart for the אוֹפַן. / ע״ס א״ב. labels.
Both pages end mid-sentence and continue on the next scans.
